newsitem.title: USA: Republicans ask probe of taped Gingrich phone call.
newsitem.headline: Republicans ask probe of taped Gingrich phone call.

text.p: House of Representatives Republicans on Friday asked Attorney General Janet Reno to investigate possible violations of federal wiretap law in connection with the secret taping of a phone call between Speaker Newt Gingrich and his top lieutenants.

The New York Times on Friday published excerpts of a taped conference call among Gingrich, other House Republicans and aides discussing a pending ethics case against the speaker last month. The paper said the call was recorded by people in Florida who are unsympathetic to Gingrich and who picked it up on a police scanner and gave the tape to an unidentified Democratic congressman.

The day of the phone call, Gingrich had agreed to concede to ethics committee findings that he had committed violations of ethics rules. The newspaper said the tape suggested he may have broken a promise to the committee concerning one of the terms of the agreement.

On Friday, Assistant House Majority Leader Tom DeLay, a Texas Republican, and House Judiciary Committee Chairman Henry Hyde, an Illinois Republican, wrote separate letters to Reno asking for a Justice Department probe of the taping, which they suggested violated federal wiretap laws. A Reno spokesman said the request would be reviewed."

"I urge you to pursue this matter with vigilance and all due haste ... This kind of abuse not only theatens the rights of those who were on that call, but of all Americans who use cellular phones on a regular basis," DeLay said. The Times said at least one of the participants used a cell phone.

Hyde said the federal wiretap act makes it a crime to intentionally intercept any wire, oral or electronic communication or to improperly disclose the contents of such improperly obtained information. Republicans said not only the persons intercepting the call, but the Democratic lawmaker who allegedly disclosed the tape, appear to have violated the act.
